items.title: Ginkgo Bioworks, OpenAI cut protein costs 40% with GPT-5 lab

featured_image.name: How Ginkgo Bioworks leverages synthetic biology to shape ...

items.description:
Ginkgo Bioworks and OpenAI announced today that their collaboration using a GPT-5-powered autonomous laboratory achieved a 40 percent reduction in cell-free protein synthesis costs, marking a milestone in the application of artificial intelligence to biological research. The biotechnology company reported the system reduced the cost of producing superfolder green fluorescent protein from $698 per gram to $422 per gram over six months of testing.[1][2][3]

The announcement, detailed in a scientific preprint not yet peer-reviewed, describes how the autonomous lab executed more than 36,000 experiments across six iterative cycles and generated nearly 150,000 data points with minimal human involvement. Human roles were primarily limited to reagent preparation, loading and unloading materials, and system oversight, while the AI managed experimental design, execution, data interpretation, and hypothesis generation.[2][4][5][3]

items.title: Study links COVID lockdowns to record methane surge

featured_image.name: COVID-19 Shutdowns Lead to Cleaner Air | AQMD Seeks to ...

items.description:
The pandemic measures that cleared city streets and grounded airplanes created an unexpected consequence: they weakened the atmosphere's ability to scrub away methane, helping to trigger the largest recorded surge in the potent greenhouse gas, according to a new study published in the journal Science.

A team of 41 scientists led by researchers at Peking University found that reductions in hydroxyl radicals during the COVID-19 period from 2020 to 2021, followed by a recovery through 2023, accounted for roughly 80 percent of the interannual variations in methane's growth rate.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump backs UK Chagos deal after reversing earlier criticism

featured_image.name: UK, US agree Chagos air base is of strategic importance after Trump criticism of deal

items.description:
President Donald Trump signaled support on Thursday for Britain's controversial agreement to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, reversing his previous sharp criticism of the deal while warning he retains the right to "militarily secure" the strategically vital Diego Garcia airbase.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he understood the agreement negotiated by Prime Minister Keir Starmer was "the best he could make," according to Reuters. The statement marks a dramatic turnaround from his January remarks when he labeled the same deal "an act of great stupidity" and "total weakness".[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Trump endorses Japan's Takaichi ahead of Sunday election

featured_image.name: Japan's snap elections: A reckless risk or calculated gamble?

items.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump threw his support behind Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Thursday, days before Japan's snap legislative election, and confirmed that the Japanese leader will visit the White House on March 19.

In a message posted on Truth Social, Trump called Takaichi "a strong, powerful, and wise Leader" who "truly loves her Country," giving what he described as his "Complete and Total Endorsement" of her and her governing coalition ahead of Sunday's vote.[1][2]

"Prime Minister Takaichi is someone who deserves powerful recognition for the job she and her Coalition are doing," Trump wrote, concluding with the all-caps rallying cry: "SHE WILL NOT LET THE PEOPLE OF JAPAN DOWN! Good luck on your very important Sunday Vote".[3]

items.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to exchange 314 prisoners at Abu Dhabi talks

featured_image.name: Russia and Ukraine agree new prisoner exchange after talks

items.description:
Delegations from the United States, Ukraine, and Russia reached an agreement on Thursday to exchange 314 prisoners of war, marking the first such exchange in five months and a tangible outcome from ongoing peace negotiations in Abu Dhabi.

US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff announced the deal on social media platform X, stating that "this outcome was achieved from peace talks that have been detailed and productive." He added that "while significant work remains, steps like this demonstrate that sustained diplomatic engagement is delivering tangible results and advancing efforts to end the war in Ukraine."[1][2]

Witkoff expressed gratitude to the United Arab Emirates for hosting the discussions and credited President Donald Trump for his leadership in making the agreement possible. The exchange represents the first prisoner swap between Moscow and Kyiv since October 2025.[3][4][1]

items.title: Black hole emits energy a trillion times greater than Death Star

featured_image.name: Black hole burps up shredded star years after consuming it ...

items.description:
A supermassive black hole has been "burping out" the remains of a shredded star for four years and is still ramping up, with scientists predicting its radio emissions will continue growing until reaching a peak in 2027.

The phenomenon, described as potentially one of the most powerful single events ever detected in the universe, has released energy estimated to be at least a trillion times greater than the fictional Death Star—and possibly closer to 100 trillion times that figure, according to research published Wednesday in the Astrophysical Journal.[1][2]

items.title: New START treaty expires as Russia shadows European satellites

featured_image.name: European Commission confirms Russia targets EU satellites and ...

items.description:
Two Russian spacecraft have intercepted communications from at least a dozen key European satellites over the past three years, European security officials told the Financial Times, as the last remaining nuclear arms control treaty between the United States and Russia expired on Wednesday.

The dual developments mark a concerning escalation in space-based tensions and the collapse of decades of nuclear restraint between the world's two largest atomic powers.

items.title: US and Russia reach informal deal as New START treaty expires

featured_image.name: Explainer: Could US and Russia extend last nuclear weapons treaty?

items.description:
UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Wednesday urged the United States and Russia to negotiate a new nuclear arms control framework "without delay" as the New START treaty expired at midnight, warning that the world now faces the highest risk of nuclear weapons use "in decades."[1][2][3]

The expiration of the 2010 agreement—which capped both nations' deployed strategic nuclear warheads at 1,550 and established verification mechanisms—marks what Guterres called "a grave moment for international peace and security." For the first time in more than 50 years, no binding limits exist on the strategic nuclear arsenals of the two nations that together possess roughly 87% of the world's nuclear weapons.[2][4][5][1]

items.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping urged President Donald Trump to handle arms sales to Taiwan "with prudence" during a phone call on Wednesday, February 4, underscoring Beijing's view that the Taiwan issue remains "the most important issue" in U.S.-China relations. The exchange, the first direct conversation between the two leaders since November, came as both sides prepared for Trump's planned April visit to Beijing.[1][2]

items.title: Wargame finds Russia could seize Lithuanian city in days

featured_image.name: Wargame simulates how Russia could take Nato country 'within days'

items.description: A tabletop military exercise conducted by former German and NATO officials in December 2025 concluded that Russia could capture the strategically vital Lithuanian city of Marijampole within days by exploiting allied indecision rather than overwhelming force. The findings, published this week, have intensified scrutiny of NATO's decision-making capabilities and political resolve in a potential crisis.
